intent: The table that dethrones the All Blacks, the stadium where it started in 1995, then the ball's long flight to the one-point final in Paris.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which nation has the MOST Rugby World Cups?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which nation has the most Rugby World Cups?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat
lines.text: New Zealand, Australia, or South Africa?
South Africa. The Springboks have lifted the Webb Ellis Cup 4 times, more than any other nation.

lines.direction: ease back over southern Africa; bars build on 'Zealand' with South Africa on top; the All Black flag-ball thinks; a rugby-ball sticker on 'England'; South Africa pulses
lines.text: The All Blacks of New Zealand have 3, Australia 2, England a single title. Nobody else has.

lines.direction: tighten on Johannesburg; the pin and tag on 'Johannesburg'; a broken-chain sticker on 'apartheid'; the 1995 card and a trophy sticker on 'Mandela'; the Springbok flag-ball grins
lines.text: The first came at home in Johannesburg in 1995, a year after apartheid ended, Nelson Mandela in a Springbok jersey.

lines.direction: pull right out so Africa and Europe share the frame; a rugby ball rides the drawn line from Johannesburg to Paris until 'Paris'; the Paris pin and tag; the 12–11 card on 'point'; the All Black flag-ball slumps
lines.text: The latest came in Paris in 2023, by a single point over New Zealand.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
